sections.content: The direct object of a verb -- the thing you want, ask for, or look for -- takes the accusative ending -t. Nouns ending in a vowel usually add -t directly, with a lengthened vowel; nouns ending in a consonant often need a linking vowel that follows vowel harmony: -at/-ot/-et/-öt.

items.spanish: Egy pólót és egy táskát keresek.
items.english: I'm looking for a T-shirt and a bag.

sections.content: Watch nouns ending in -a or -e: they lengthen before -t. táska (bag) becomes táskát, not 'táskat'. When in doubt, say the noun out loud with -t added and see which vowel sounds natural.
